memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Moabites said to the elders of Midian, "This horde is going to lick up everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field." So Balak son of Zippor, who was king of Moab at that time, sent messengers to summon Balaam son of Beor, who was at Pethor, near the Euphrates River, in his native land. - Num 22:4-5a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Gripped by fear, Balak looks for a solution. But instead of seeking peace or turning to the true God, he sends far away for Balaam, a man known for pronouncing blessings and curses. Balak believes that if he can hire the right spiritual power, he can defeat Israel with words.

This is the choice of a desperate heart that does not know God. Rather than examining whether he stood against the Lord's purposes, Balak looked for a spiritual weapon to use for his own ends. He treated blessing and cursing as tools to be bought, as if God's favour could be purchased and directed at will.

We can fall into a similar trap. When trouble comes, we sometimes look for the right technique, the right person, the right formula to fix our problem, rather than humbling ourselves before God. We want power on our terms instead of surrender on His.

The gospel calls us in a different direction entirely. We do not manipulate God; we come to Him through Christ in humble faith. There is no formula to master, only a Saviour to trust. When you are afraid, do not go searching for the wrong kind of help. Go to the Father who welcomes you in Jesus (Heb 4:16).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When trouble comes, do you seek God or search for a quick fix?
2. Have you ever treated God's blessing as something to control?
3. What would it look like to bring your fear to God in humble trust?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from seeking help in all the wrong places. When I am afraid, draw me to come humbly to You through Jesus rather than trusting in my own schemes. Amen.
